::: {#def-graph .theorem}
## Network graph

An ordered pair $\mathscr{G} = (\mathcal{N}, \psi)$ with node set $\mathcal{N}$, whose elements represent [observational units](#def-observational-unit), and adjacency function $\psi$, which represents potential causal influence between observational units. The network is directed: the adjacency function assigns a nonnegative weight $\psi(i,j)$ to each ordered pair of distinct observational units, the weight of $j$'s influence on $i$, and $\psi(i,j)$ need not equal $\psi(j,i)$.

$$
\mathscr G=(\mathcal N,\psi),\qquad \psi:\mathcal N\times\mathcal N\to \mathbb R_{\ge 0},\qquad \psi(i,i)=0
$$

$j$ influences $i$ if and only if $\psi(i,j) > 0$.

The **neighborhood** of an observational unit $i \in \mathcal N$ is the set of units that influence it:

$$
\mathcal{N}_i = \{ j \in \mathcal{N} : \psi(i,j) > 0 \}.
$$

The **network weights** $\boldsymbol\Psi_i$ of unit $i$ are the $i$th row of the adjacency matrix, the weights of every unit's influence on $i$, with $n = |\mathcal N|$:

$$
\boldsymbol\Psi_i = [\psi(i,1), \dots, \psi(i,n)]^T.
$$

For a covariate $\mathbf X$, the **network values** $\mathbf X_{\mathcal N_i}$ are the entries of $\mathbf X$ belonging to the neighborhood of $i$:

$$
\mathbf X_{\mathcal N_i}=\big(X_j\big)_{j\in \mathcal N_i}.
$$
:::
